functions.reason: cel-spec's standard definitions over strings are size, startsWith, endsWith, matches, contains and concatenation, and nothing else; the strings extension has an equivalent, which Telo does not ship. This member differs from it: despite its name it lowercases every letter the host language's own casing lowercases, not the ASCII letters alone, so 'TacoCÆt'.lowerAscii() answers 'tacocæt' where the extension answers 'tacocÆt'. Kept, with that behaviour, for the manifests already written against it

cel-spec's standard definitions over strings are size, startsWith, endsWith, matches, contains and concatenation, and nothing else; the strings extension has an equivalent, which Telo does not ship. This member differs from it: indices are UTF-16 CODE UNITS, not code points, so a string holding a character outside the basic plane is indexed differently than the extension indexes it — a port that read this member as the extension's would index by rune and silently change the answer of every manifest that cuts a string. Kept for the manifests already written against it

symmetricOperators.description: Equality is declared per type: two values of unrelated types are not compared, and an optional is not compared at all.
CEL orders every scalar type. A list and a map are comparable for equality alone.

crossNumericOperators.reason: CEL's checker is strict about the numeric types — its own suite writes dyn(1) < 2u precisely because of that — so ordering across them is an extension of what the language accepts at check time, kept because manifests rely on it. It never computes across them, and equality across them stays refused.
